name: Architecture and Design
blurb: Công trình, vật liệu, thiết kế

words.definitionEn: a tall, vertical structure used as a support in a building or as an ornamental feature
words.example: The ancient Greek temple featured massive marble columns that supported the roof.

words.definitionEn: the lowest load-bearing part of a building, typically below ground level
words.example: The architect ensured the foundation was reinforced to withstand earthquakes.

words.meaningVi: bố trí, sơ đồ mặt bằng
words.definitionEn: the way in which the parts of a building or structure are arranged
words.example: The open-plan layout of the office encourages collaboration among employees.

words.definitionEn: a very tall building with many floors
words.example: The city's skyline is dominated by modern skyscrapers made of glass and steel.

words.definitionEn: a building or other object constructed from several parts
words.example: The steel structure of the bridge was designed to withstand high winds.

words.definitionEn: the front or outer face of a building
words.example: The historic building's facade was carefully restored to preserve its original appearance.

words.definitionEn: a detailed plan or drawing of a building or structure
words.example: Before construction begins, the architect must finalize the blueprint for the project.

words.definitionEn: relating to design that minimizes environmental impact
words.example: Sustainable architecture incorporates energy-efficient materials and renewable energy sources.

words.definitionEn: the process of repairing and improving a building
words.example: The renovation of the old factory into loft apartments attracted many young professionals.

words.definitionEn: concerned with the beauty or artistic quality of a building
words.example: The aesthetic appeal of the house was enhanced by its large windows and natural stone walls.

words.definitionEn: a rounded vault forming the roof of a building
words.example: The cathedral's impressive dome can be seen from miles away.

words.definitionEn: the quality of being made up of exactly similar parts facing each other
words.example: The symmetry of the building's design gives it a sense of balance and harmony.

words.definitionEn: the basic physical systems and structures needed for a city or building to function
words.example: Urban infrastructure includes roads, water supply, and sewage systems.

words.definitionEn: a building or structure that is easily recognizable and historically significant
words.example: The Sydney Opera House is one of the most famous landmarks in the world.

words.definitionEn: a long, sturdy piece of timber or metal used as a horizontal support in a building
words.example: The wooden beams in the ceiling were exposed to create a rustic atmosphere.

words.definitionEn: a curved structure spanning an opening, often used as a decorative or supportive element
words.example: The Roman arch is a classic architectural feature still used in modern buildings.

words.definitionEn: manufactured in advance in sections that can be easily transported and assembled on site
words.example: Prefabricated houses are becoming more popular due to their lower cost and faster construction time.

words.definitionEn: buildings and structures of historical or cultural importance
words.example: The city's heritage buildings are protected by law to prevent demolition.

words.definitionEn: the division of land into areas for different uses, such as residential, commercial, or industrial
words.example: Zoning regulations determine what types of buildings can be constructed in each district.

words.definitionEn: the outline of buildings and structures against the sky
words.example: The new skyscraper will dramatically alter the city's skyline.

words.definitionEn: decorated with many intricate details, often in a lavish style
words.example: The ornate ceiling of the ballroom was covered in gold leaf and intricate frescoes.

words.definitionEn: using simple, clean lines and a lack of unnecessary decoration
words.example: Minimalist architecture emphasizes functionality and simplicity over ornamentation.

words.definitionEn: a large, imposing building
words.example: The grand edifice of the parliament building symbolizes the nation's power and history.

words.definitionEn: a long projecting beam or structure fixed at one end only, often used in modern architecture
words.example: The cantilever of the balcony allows it to extend outward without visible supports.

words.definitionEn: architecture that uses local materials and traditional styles, reflecting the culture of a region
words.example: Vernacular architecture is often more sustainable because it adapts to the local climate and resources.

words.meaningVi: giếng trời, không gian mở trung tâm
words.definitionEn: a large open central space in a building, often with a glass roof
words.example: The hotel's atrium features a stunning glass ceiling and tropical plants.

words.definitionEn: a thin wall or screen used to divide a room
words.example: The office uses glass partitions to create private workstations.

words.definitionEn: a material applied to the outside of a building to provide insulation or protection
words.example: The building's aluminum cladding gives it a modern appearance.

words.definitionEn: a projecting support built against a wall to strengthen it
words.example: The Gothic cathedral has flying buttresses that support the high walls.

words.definitionEn: supporting the weight of a structure
words.example: Removing a load-bearing wall without proper reinforcement can be dangerous.

words.meaningVi: không gian mở, ít vách ngăn
words.definitionEn: having a large open area with few or no walls
words.example: Many modern offices adopt an open-plan layout to encourage collaboration.

words.meaningVi: cải tạo, trang bị thêm hệ thống mới cho công trình cũ
words.definitionEn: the process of adding new features or systems to an existing building
words.example: Retrofitting older buildings with energy-efficient systems is a key aspect of sustainable architecture.

words.definitionEn: relating to space
words.example: The architect's spatial arrangement of rooms ensures a smooth flow of movement.

words.definitionEn: material used to prevent heat, sound, or electricity from passing through
words.example: Proper insulation in walls reduces energy consumption significantly.

words.definitionEn: the provision of fresh air to a space
words.example: Good ventilation is essential in high-rise buildings to maintain air quality.

words.definitionEn: the study of designing equipment and spaces for efficient and comfortable human use
words.example: The design of the kitchen prioritizes ergonomics, with countertops at a comfortable height.

words.definitionEn: consisting of separate units that can be combined or arranged
words.example: Modular construction allows for faster building assembly and customization.

words.definitionEn: concrete with embedded steel bars for added strength
words.example: Reinforced concrete is widely used in high-rise buildings due to its high load-bearing capacity.

words.definitionEn: relating to earthquakes
words.example: Buildings in seismic zones must be designed to withstand strong ground motions.

words.meaningVi: cảnh quan, thiết kế cảnh quan
words.definitionEn: the process of improving the appearance of an area of land by planting trees, shrubs, etc.
words.example: The landscaping around the office complex includes a pond and native plants.

words.definitionEn: a window in a roof or ceiling
words.example: The skylight in the living room floods the space with natural light.

words.definitionEn: an entrance hall or lobby
words.example: The hotel's grand foyer is decorated with marble floors and chandeliers.

words.definitionEn: a row of evenly spaced columns supporting a roof
words.example: The colonnade along the front of the building provides a shaded walkway.

words.meaningVi: trán tường (hình tam giác) kiểu cổ điển
words.definitionEn: a triangular gable above a doorway or window in classical architecture
words.example: The pediment of the bank building is adorned with a sculpture.

words.definitionEn: a platform projecting from the wall of a building
words.example: The apartment's balcony offers a panoramic view of the city.

words.definitionEn: a lift for moving people or goods between floors
words.example: The building has four elevators to handle the high volume of occupants.

words.definitionEn: a set of stairs
words.example: The grand staircase in the mansion is made of marble.

words.meaningVi: nhà kính, phòng kính trồng cây
words.definitionEn: a room with glass walls and roof for growing plants
words.example: The conservatory is attached to the main house and serves as a winter garden.

words.definitionEn: a luxurious apartment on the top floor of a building
words.example: The penthouse features a private rooftop terrace and floor-to-ceiling windows.

words.definitionEn: a low-ceilinged floor between two main floors
words.example: The library has a mezzanine level that overlooks the main reading room.
